annotations.label: macOS 26.6 → 27
annotations.description: macOS runners were updated from macOS 26.6 to 27, and from then on did not use the object cache until JuliaCI/sandboxed-buildkite-agent#176

annotations.label: TTFX driver #634
annotations.description: The TTFX driver instruments the task script for per-phase gc and compile stats and repeats it with the GC off (julia-buildkite#634). Its added statements cost about a millisecond of run on every task until julia-buildkite#635.

annotations.label: TTFX driver #635
annotations.description: The TTFX driver keeps its instrumentation out of the timed windows (julia-buildkite#635), removing the fixed cost of about a millisecond of run per task that julia-buildkite#634 had added.

annotations.label: GPUArrays 12 / JLArrays 0.4
annotations.description: The JLArrays task resolved the newly registered GPUArrays v12.0.0 and JLArrays v0.4.0. Its load went from 0.9 s to 8.4 s (1.8 GB allocated, no extra compile time) and its precompile from 17.5 s to 27.2 s. The other tasks did not change, so this is not a Julia regression.

annotations.label: macOS object cache
annotations.description: The macOS agents use the object cache again, which they had stopped using with the update to macOS 27. The warm runs are about a third faster from this job on, the suite geomean going from about 0.61 s to 0.40 s.

annotations.label: TTFX driver #664
annotations.description: The TTFX driver loads freshly precompiled packages once in an untimed process before measuring, so load no longer includes a cost paid once per precompile. The load suite geomean went from about 0.38 s to 0.23 s, level with the GC-off repeats, which never paid it.

annotations.label: DocStringExtensions 0.10
annotations.description: Five tasks resolved new package versions, among them DocStringExtensions 0.10, whose release made the package slower to precompile. Their precompile rose by 12% to 53% (ForwardDiff 4.7 s to 7.1 s). The tasks whose packages did not change held level, so the Julia commit of this build (#63813) is not the cause.

annotations.label: GMT 1.44.1
annotations.description: The GMT task resolved the newly registered GMT v1.44.1, which no longer depends on SparseArrays. Loaded alone, GMT now invalidates 3 MethodInstances instead of 599 and loads about 0.2 s faster. With the stdlibs loaded first, SparseArrays invalidates GMT's precompiled plotting code, so the first plot recompiles it: the stdlibs-first run went from 0.008 s to 5.9 s. Importing SparseArrays alone before GMT reproduces this locally, and v1.44.0 does not show it. The Julia commit of this build (#63909) is not the cause.
